name: Augmented Hill-Climb
one_liner: A reinforcement-learning rule that trains a molecule generator on the top scorers per batch, so costly scores like docking are used less.

loop.proposes: SMILES strings from an RNN (also tested on a transformer) molecule generator
loop.judged_by: A scoring function evaluated on each sampled batch; the paper's tasks include docking objectives, with diversity filters
loop.steers: RL updates the generator with a hybrid of REINVENT's loss and Hill-Climb's top-scorer selection

headline_result: On the authors' benchmark tasks, compared with REINVENT, optimization ability improved about 1.5-fold and sample efficiency about 45-fold, and Augmented Hill-Climb outperformed the other reinforcement learning strategies tested on six tasks.
caveat: The gains are measured on the authors' benchmark tasks and docking objectives, not on lab-measured activity. It is a training rule inside the REINVENT-style setup rather than a separate system.
beyond_harness_note: The generator is a SMILES RNN or transformer whose weights are updated by the score, with docking-style scoring as the judge.
generative_model: SMILES RNN (and RL-stabilized transformer), updated by reinforcement learning
algorithmic_authority: Task scoring functions including docking, plus diversity filters

sources.title: Augmented Hill-Climb increases reinforcement learning efficiency for language-based de novo molecule generation (J Cheminformatics 14, 2022)

verification.notes: Abstract opened via Europe PMC (PMC9531503; the Springer URL redirects). Authors Thomas, O'Boyle, Bender, de Graaf; first-author affiliation printed as Centre for Molecular Informatics, University of Cambridge (org field uses that only). Numbers (1.5-fold, 45-fold, six tasks, transformer result) quoted from the abstract. The draft's 'better sample efficiency than REINVENT's strategy' is correct and now carries the ~45-fold figure. Only the abstract was read, not the full methods.
